newsitem.title: UK: IGC sees sharp fall in world durum wheat crop.
newsitem.headline: IGC sees sharp fall in world durum wheat crop.

text.p: World production of durum wheat is likely to fall by about five million tonnes this year to below 29 million tonnes, according to the International Grains Council.

In its Grains Market Report, out on Thursday, the IGC blamed lower output in the EU, "confirmation that Algeria's grain harvest was the lowest in 20 years," and a first official forecast in the US which placed the crop almost a third below the 1996 level.
The EU crop is expected to fall by around 10 percent. "Output appears to have fallen significantly in Italy, Spain and France," the IGC said.

Earlier this month the official Algerian news agency APS said Algeria's cereal harvest will fall to a 20-year low of about 1.05 million tonnes in 1996/97 due to drought, after a record 4.9 million crop the previous season.
Some 75 percent of Algeria's wheat crop is durum and the country is one of the world's leading durum importers. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
